source.title: Confluent Cloud APIs
source.mutability: The vendor-hosted current URL is mutable. Generation fails closed unless its bytes and SHA-256 match this reviewed aggregate contract.

cloud-api-key.description: Authenticate with Cloud API Keys using HTTP Basic Auth. Treat the Cloud API Key ID as the username and Cloud API Key Secret as the password.

confluent-sts-access-token.description: Authenticate with Confluent API using this credentials (JSON Web Tokens) following OAuth 2.0.

global-api-key.description: Authenticate with Global API Keys using HTTP Basic Auth. Treat the Global API Key ID as the username and Global API Key Secret as the password.

resource-api-key.description: Authenticate with resource-specific API Keys using HTTP Basic Auth. Treat the resource-specific API Key ID as the username and resource-specific API Key Secret as the password.

external-access-token.description: Authenticate with Confluent API using this credentials (JSON Web Tokens) following OAuth 2.0.

oauth.description: Authenticate with OAuth 2.0. Currently this is only supported for partner APIs.

source_decision.reason: Confluent exposes infrastructure, streaming, schema, catalog, SQL, identity, network, and billing resources. Kafka records and Flink results are arbitrary customer data rather than semantically honest Recued tasks, notes, or projects, and the aggregate authority proves no durable version plus deletion contract for such a Source.

audit_findings_folded.finding: The aggregate contract spans four origins and incompatible Cloud, resource, partner, and no-auth credential models.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Split the suite into eleven one-ingredient leaves over seven separately enrolled connection profiles; no credential is replayed across an origin or auth family.

audit_findings_folded.finding: One provider-share image upload requires arbitrary image/* request bytes, but the REST binding has no file_ref-to-binary upload mode.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Excluded exactly that operation instead of corrupting binary bytes through a text body; all other current operations remain admitted.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Two Connect OpenAPI path keys illegally embed fixed query text for response expansion and sensitive-field masking.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Preserved each exact openapi_path for documentary proof while moving expand=info,status,id and mask_sensitive=true into immutable runtime static_query entries.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Twenty-two Schema Registry Data Catalog operations omit security even though the same aggregate authority says unauthenticated API requests fail.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Kept them on the Schema Registry endpoint and resource-key connection, and made the documentary discrepancy explicit rather than declaring them public.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Nine exporter operations advertise only application/vnd.schemaregistry.v1+json, while the current connection adapter JSON-parses only application/json.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Admitted the calls with their exact vendor media and an honest string response contract; no object result_path or parsed-JSON claim is made.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Confluent says page-size limits are dynamic and page_size is valid only on the first request, but automatic replay reuses first-page inputs.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Withheld both page_size and page_token from callers and walks only the opaque page_token extracted from metadata.next, using provider defaults and no invented maximum.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Only eighteen of 165 admitted request bodies set requestBody.required even though the operations need a payload.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Requires every JSON body as bounded complete body_raw and preserves nested JSON verbatim; the STS form exposes only dynamic fields and locks its three RFC 8693 constants.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Unbounded OpenAPI integer parameters can exceed JavaScript's exact-number range.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Projects every unbounded integer parameter to a validated exact decimal string and enables unsafe-integer response preservation on parsed JSON operations.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Fifty-two admitted array parameters omit a provider maximum, but the closed request-schema gate requires an explicit collection bound.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Applies a Recued 256-item request safety ceiling, preserves repeated-key serialization, and never presents that implementation bound as a Confluent limit.

audit_findings_folded.finding: Seven srcm/v2 operations are explicitly provider-deprecated.
audit_findings_folded.resolution: Records and excludes the exact deprecated set while retaining current srcm/v3 coverage.

official_operations.exclusion_reason: Confluent serves these on a separate regional SQL origin and labels them v1alpha1. Admitting them requires a seventh connection profile the user would have to enrol independently, which is a connection-shape decision rather than a document re-pin. Re-admit once the surface leaves alpha.

The official request body is image/* binary data. The catalog REST binding accepts JSON, structured form scalars, or a literal text body but has no file_ref-to-binary request transport. Admitting it would corrupt arbitrary image bytes, so the operation remains excluded until binary request upload is a declared binding capability.

Confluent keys this route WITH a query string — `…/config/translate?mask_sensitive=true` — which is malformed OpenAPI, and unlike its sibling `…/connectors?expand=…` there is NO clean `…/config/translate` key in the document. The operation is therefore unprovable by construction: the publish op-prover matches (method, path) against the document's own keys, and the only key naming this route is one no path may legally have. Excluded rather than shipped unprovable, which blocks publish for the whole pack. No recipe in the corpus referenced it (checked against a known-positive grep). Re-admit it the moment Confluent keys the route without the query text.
